label: Community impact
description: Articulate significant, measurable impact on Alaska communities commensurate with a Legacy-scale award.

scoring.desc: Impact is aspirational and not tied to measurable outcomes.
Impact is described for a specific population but outcomes are output-level not outcome-level.
Impact includes baseline data, quantified beneficiaries, and a theory of change with evaluation plan.

common_failures: Impact framed as activities rather than outcomes

label: Organizational capacity
description: Demonstrate leadership, staffing, and governance capable of stewarding a multi-year, high-dollar award.

scoring.desc: Organization has limited track record at this scale and leadership plan is thin.
Organization has managed awards of similar scope but succession or key-person risk is unaddressed.
Organization has clear track record at scale, named leadership, succession plans, and board oversight.

common_failures: No prior awards at comparable scale
Board not engaged with the initiative

label: Financial management
description: Show audited financials, internal controls, and ability to manage large draw-downs and reporting.

scoring.desc: No audit, qualified audit, or material control weaknesses.
Clean audit but limited experience managing awards of this size.
Clean audit, documented internal controls, and prior experience drawing down federal or large foundation funds.

label: Community partnerships
description: Document meaningful partnerships with community, tribal, government, or peer organizations that will co-deliver the work.

scoring.desc: Partners are named but roles and commitments are unclear.
Partners have defined roles but no MOUs or letters of support attached.
Partners have signed MOUs or letters, clear roles, and shared decision-making structures.

common_failures: Partner letters that are generic endorsements
No tribal consultation for projects in tribal communities
Partner roles that duplicate applicant roles

label: Project feasibility and sustainability
description: Show the project is executable on the proposed timeline and that outcomes persist beyond the award period.

scoring.desc: Timeline is aggressive and no post-award sustainability plan exists.
Timeline is credible but sustainability relies on a single uncommitted funding source.
Timeline is credible with milestones and sustainability is diversified across revenue, partnerships, or policy change.

common_failures: Sustainability plan is a future grant application
No operations and maintenance plan for capital projects

label: Alignment with community and state needs
description: Connect the project to documented Alaska community priorities and state-level needs assessments.

scoring.desc: Needs are cited from one source but community voice is not present.
Needs are triangulated across community input, data sources, and state or regional plans.

common_failures: Quoting national statistics without Alaska-specific data
No community voice or listening sessions cited
Duplicating existing services without a gap analysis
